The '''2009–10 Primeira Liga''' (also known as the '''Liga Sagres''' for sponsorship reasons) was the 76th season of the [[Primeira Liga]], the top professional league for Portuguese [[association football]] clubs. It began on 16 August 2009 and ended on 9 May 2010.

[[S.L. Benfica|Benfica]] won their 32nd league title after a 2–1 home victory over [[Rio Ave F.C.|Rio Ave]] on the last matchday.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://int.soccerway.com/news/2010/May/09/benfica-win-portuguese-championship/|title=Benfica win Portuguese championship|date=9 May 2010|work=Soccerway|publisher=Global Sports Media|access-date=10 May 2010|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20100512194428/http://www.soccerway.com/news/2010/May/09/benfica-win-portuguese-championship/|archive-date= 12 May 2010|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.uefa.com/memberassociations/association=por/news/newsid=1486467.html |title=Cardozo seals title for Benfica |date=9 May 2010 |work=[[UEFA]] |access-date=10 May 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100511104824/http://www.uefa.com/memberassociations/association%3Dpor/news/newsid%3D1486467.html |archive-date=11 May 2010 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Benfica striker [[Óscar Cardozo]] was the top scorer with 26 goals.

==Changes from 2008–09==

===Team changes===
[[C.D. Trofense|Trofense]] have been relegated to the [[Liga de Honra]] after finishing the [[Portuguese Liga 2008–09|2008–09 season]] in 16th and last place. Trofense were to be accompanied by [[C.F. Os Belenenses|Belenenses]], who finished in 15th place. Belenenses were ending a ten-year stretch in the Portuguese top-level league, while Trofense returned to the Liga da Honra after just one year in the top flight.

[[C.F. Estrela da Amadora|Estrela da Amadora]], however, who finished last season in 11th place, have been relegated for economic problems to the Liga Vitalis. Therefore, Belenenses' relegation has been reversed and they will participate in the Liga Sagres once more.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.maisfutebol.iol.pt/belenenses/e-amadora-liga-belenenses-inscricao/1072743-1463.html|title=Registration of E. Amadora rejected, Belenenses is in Liga|date=30 June 2009|publisher=Mais futebol|language=pt|access-date=19 July 2009|archive-date=3 July 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090703012546/http://www.maisfutebol.iol.pt/belenenses/e-amadora-liga-belenenses-inscricao/1072743-1463.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

The relegated teams were replaced by [[Liga de Honra 2008–09|Liga Vitalis 2008–09]] champions [[S.C. Olhanense|Olhanense]] and runners-up [[U.D. Leiria|União de Leiria]]. Olhanense returned to the top-flight after 34 years, while Leiria was back after a one-year hiatus.

===Structural changes===
Based on [[UEFA coefficients]], Portugal finished in tenth place of the UEFA country ranking after the 2008–09 season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.xs4all.nl/~kassiesa/bert/uefa/data/method4/crank2009.html|title=UEFA Country Ranking 2009|last=Kassies|first=Bert|access-date=25 May 2009}}</ref> As a result, the Portuguese league will lose one qualification spot for the [[2010–11 UEFA Europa League]]. The third-placed team will now qualify for the [[2010–11 UEFA Europa League#Third qualification round|third qualification round]] instead of the play-off round. The fourth-placed team will enter the competition in the [[2010–11 UEFA Europa League#Second qualification round|second qualification round]] while the fifth place will not initially qualify for any European competitions via league placement. However, this may change during the course of the season depending on the league performance of both [[2009–10 Taça de Portugal|2009–10 Cup of Portugal]] finalists.

=== Annual awards ===

==== LPFP Primeira Liga Player of the Year ====
The [[LPFP Primeira Liga Player of the Year]] was awarded to [[David Luiz]] of [[S.L. Benfica|Benfica]].<ref name="1LPFP10">{{cite web | url=http://www.cnid.pt/index.php?option=com_content&task=view&id=128&Itemid=38 | title=Rosa Mota e Carlos Lopes Recebem Prémio Fernando Soromenho |trans-title=Rosa Mota e Carlos Lopes Receive Fernando Soromenho Award | publisher=CNID | date=25 May 2010 | access-date=27 May 2010 | language=pt}}</ref>

==== LPFP Primeira Liga Breakthrough Player of the Year ====
The [[LPFP Awards#Players Awards|LPFP Primeira Liga Breakthrough Player of the Year]] was awarded to [[Fábio Coentrão]] of Benfica.<ref name="1LPFP10"/>

==== LPFP Primeira Liga Manager of the Year ====
The [[LPFP Awards#Coaches Awards|LPFP Primeira Liga Manager of the Year]] was awarded to [[Jorge Jesus]] of Benfica.<ref name="1LPFP10"/>

==== LPFP Primeira Liga Breakthrough Manager of the Year ====
The [[LPFP Awards#Coaches Awards|LPFP Primeira Liga Breakthrough Manager of the Year]] was awarded to [[André Villas-Boas]] of [[Associação Académica de Coimbra – O.A.F.|Académica]].<ref name="1LPFP10"/>
